behaviors.label: Write files
behaviors.description: Master gate for file writes (Write, Edit). Set to deny/ask to shut writing off everywhere. WHERE writes are allowed is set by write-scope; this behavior deliberately emits no unscoped rule of its own, because a bare Write/Edit entry would out-rank every path-scoped rule and silently defeat the scoping.

behaviors.label: Read files
behaviors.description: Master gate for file reads. WHERE reads are allowed is set by read-scope. Harnesses that cannot express path scoping (Gemini's Policy Engine) fall back to this whole-tool decision.

behaviors.label: Read scope
behaviors.description: Where files may be read without prompting: agent scratch directories, which are correct to read whichever repository is in use. Reads inside the current repository are covered by the repository boundary; paths outside both prompt.

behaviors.label: Write scope
behaviors.description: Where files may be written without prompting regardless of which repository is in use: the temp dirs agent scratch work lands in. Writes inside the current repository are decided by the repository boundary, not by this list, so no personal directory layout belongs here.

behaviors.label: Read credential files
behaviors.description: Credential material that is never correct for an agent to read, denied everywhere including inside the current repository. This is the one layer the repository boundary cannot provide: a .env inside your checkout is in-bounds for repo-write-boundary, so only a deny rule stops it. Claude ranks deny above every allow, so these out-rank both the scope allows and the boundary hook. Deny is not a prompt — there is no in-session override; carve out a path here rather than working around it. The .env variants are enumerated rather than globbed as .env.* so that .env.example and .env.sample stay readable: they are committed template files carrying placeholder values, and are often the fastest way to learn what a project expects. Claude permission rules have no negation, so a readable exception must be expressed as a narrower deny, not an allow that would be out-ranked. A new secret-bearing variant therefore needs adding here explicitly. readableExceptions are public certificate-authority bundles the *.pem pattern would otherwise hide: TLS clients such as curl and npm read them to verify servers, so a sandboxed shell command could reach no host without them. They hold no secrets. They are re-allowed only where a shell sandbox can carve a path out of a denied pattern (Claude's); file-tool deny rules still cover them.

behaviors.label: Edit the plans store directly
behaviors.description: Write or edit files in a repo's plans store worktree (`repo_plans`). Plans change only through `roborepo plans` commands, which validate, commit, and push; a direct edit skips all three and the next store command refuses it. Denied for Claude, whose writes inside the repo's worktree family otherwise need no prompt. Codex cannot take this rule, because the CLI it runs writes there from inside its sandbox.

behaviors.label: Repository boundary
behaviors.description: Writes inside the repository you are working in proceed; writes outside it follow this setting. Reads are wider: the whole repository family (a worktree, its primary checkout, and its sibling worktrees) is readable, because comparing a branch against main is routine while writing across checkouts is how one session clobbers another's work. Enforced at tool-call time for harnesses with hooks, so the boundary is the current checkout rather than a fixed directory. Claude enforces this with a PreToolUse hook; Codex with a managed-workspace permission profile, whose runtime workspace root is augmented by the current repo's worktree root from its plans config.

behaviors.label: Sandboxed shell commands
behaviors.description: Run each shell command inside the OS sandbox, which confines writes to the current repository, the temp folders in Write scope, and the npm cache, keeps Read credential files unreadable, and sends network traffic through Reach allowed hosts. Allow runs sandboxed commands without prompting, whatever their shape (pipes, loops, inline scripts), unless an ask or deny rule names them; ask keeps the sandbox but prompts by the command rules; deny turns the sandbox off. Docker, gh, the git network commands, and roborepo cannot work inside it, so a call made only of those runs outside it under the command rules. A call that adds any other command, a pipe included, stays sandboxed. Codex always sandboxes its commands, so this applies to Claude only.

behaviors.label: Delete files
behaviors.description: Remove files from disk (rm, git rm).

behaviors.label: Go online
behaviors.description: Codex's sandbox network switch: on or off for every host. Claude's shell sandbox reads the separate allowed-host list instead, so this switch never makes Claude network commands prompt.

behaviors.label: Reach allowed hosts
behaviors.description: Hosts a sandboxed shell command may reach without prompting: the npm registry and GitHub over HTTPS. Allow lets them through; ask makes them prompt like any other host; deny refuses them. Hosts missing from the list prompt. Git over SSH cannot pass the sandbox proxy, so the git network commands run outside the sandbox (see Sandboxed shell commands).

behaviors.label: Commit code
behaviors.description: Stage and commit changes locally (git add, git commit).

behaviors.label: Push code
behaviors.description: Send commits to a remote (git push). Prompts by default. Where the protected-branch hooks are installed, they approve pushes they verify land on a non-protected branch and deny the rest, so agents push to feature branches without a prompt; force variants are denied separately by rewrite-history.

behaviors.label: Pull code
behaviors.description: Bring remote changes into the working tree (git pull). Prompts because a pull can merge or rebase in-flight work.

behaviors.label: Switch branches
behaviors.description: Change the checked-out branch (git checkout, git switch). Prompts because it moves the working tree out from under in-flight work.

behaviors.label: Rewrite published history
behaviors.description: Force-push or otherwise overwrite remote history. Denied outright — recovery depends on someone else still holding the old objects.

behaviors.label: Check out the main branch
behaviors.description: Move the working tree onto main. Denied so agent work stays on feature branches. Prefix-matched, so it is a guardrail against the common form, not an airtight block.

behaviors.label: Read GitHub
behaviors.description: Look at pull requests and CI runs (gh pr view/list/status/checks/diff, gh run list/view, gh repo view). Read-only.

behaviors.label: Open pull requests
behaviors.description: Open a pull request (gh pr create). Allowed because opening a PR changes no branch: merging is denied by change-github-directly. Push the branch first with git push and pass --head, so gh neither pushes nor forks on its own.

behaviors.label: Post to GitHub
behaviors.description: Write where other people read it: comment on, edit, review, close or reopen a pull request, or open and comment on issues. Prompts, since it speaks for you.

behaviors.label: Change GitHub directly
behaviors.description: Act on GitHub without git: merge a pull request, call the API (which can rewrite main), print the auth token, or change repository settings, secrets, variables, releases, or workflows. Denied, because none of it passes through the protected-branch hooks; only GitHub branch protection covers it.

behaviors.label: Run output-capped commands
behaviors.description: The agent-facing runner: `roborepo agent-run` caps output AND validates its argv against this manifest before spawning (see scripts/cli/agent-run-policy.mjs). Plain `roborepo run` is deliberately NOT listed here — it spawns whatever it is given, and Claude's prefix matcher cannot see past the wrapper, so allowlisting it would silently override every deny/ask bucket below.

behaviors.label: Inspect roborepo state
behaviors.description: Read-only roborepo namespaces (doctor, telemetry, git, index, config show, plans validate/repair, package list/inspect/status/validate). Safe to run unattended; none of them mutate config.

behaviors.label: Read and change plans
behaviors.description: The named roborepo plans commands: read, save, order, approve, lifecycle moves, and their gates. These are the only way plan files change: each one validates the change and commits it to the plans branch, so an agent needs neither direct writes to the plans worktree nor arbitrary Git commands there.

behaviors.label: Change harness configuration
behaviors.description: roborepo namespaces that rewrite generated config or installed state (update, maintenance, mcp, package enable/disable/reconcile/adopt-live/manage/dev, skill, config set). Prompts. Anything NOT listed here — including namespaces added later — falls through to a prompt by default, so new subcommands never silently gain access.
